context: Tests a review of a routine change (an optional limit query parameter): the reviewer should find the off-by-one in the cap and the unhandled zero and negative values, judge their severity proportionately, note what the tests miss, and treat the change as routine rather than inflating it.

checklist.name: Off-by-one cap found
checklist.description: The report finds that `if n > maxLimit+1` lets a limit of 101 through uncapped, so the documented cap of 100 is not enforced, with file and line

checklist.name: Zero and negative limits found
checklist.description: The report finds that limit=0 or a negative limit is accepted and passed to the query (LIMIT 0 returns nothing; a negative LIMIT is an error or unbounded depending on the database), and suggests rejecting or defaulting them

checklist.name: Test gaps named
checklist.description: The report points out that TestParseLimit does not cover 101, 0, negative or non-numeric input, so it could not catch the defects above

checklist.name: Proportionate severity
checklist.description: None of these findings is a Blocker: they are Major at most (the cap) and Minor otherwise; the report does not claim a security or data-loss risk the diff does not have

checklist.name: No false SQL injection
checklist.description: The LIMIT $2 parameter is not reported as SQL injection; the query is parameterised

checklist.name: Pinned revision
checklist.description: The report states the reviewed revision as head 9f8e7d6c5b4a and base aa11bb22cc33

checklist.name: Report shape
checklist.description: The report has the sections Blockers, Major, Minor and nits, Retracted on review, Validation and limits, and Open questions for the author, in that order, and nothing follows the last one
